# `try_to_time`

<!-- @generated by `cargo xtask docs-sql`; do not edit. -->

Parses the `str` expression with the `format` expression to a time.
If `format` is malformed or its application does not result in a well formed time, the function
returns NULL. By default, it follows casting rules to a time if the `format` is omitted.

**Applies to:** Krishiv 0.2.0 and above. Spark: 4.1 and later.

## Syntax

```text
try_to_time(str[, format])
```

## Details

| | |
|---|---|
| Krishiv | Implemented |
| Group | `datetime_funcs` |
| Kind | scalar (function) |
| Added in Spark | 4.1.0 |
| In Spark profiles | 4.1 and later |
| Arguments | [1, 2] |
| Deterministic | yes |

## Examples

```sql
-- try_to_time, example 1
> SELECT try_to_time('00:12:00.001');
00:12:00.001
```

```sql
-- try_to_time, example 2
> SELECT try_to_time('12.10.05.999999', 'HH.mm.ss.SSSSSS');
12:10:05.999999
```

```sql
-- try_to_time, example 3
> SELECT try_to_time('foo', 'HH:mm:ss');
NULL
```
